evidence.claim: Buhari said it was his last Democracy Day speech, promised a peaceful and transparent transfer to a new president in 2023, praised 2022 party primaries as peaceful and orderly, and said aggrieved actors sought judicial justice rather than violence.
evidence.title: President Buhari’s Democracy Day Speech
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said it was his last Democracy Day speech, promised a peaceful and transparent transfer to a new president in 2023, praised 2022 party primaries as peaceful and orderly, and said aggrieved actors sought judicial justice rather than violence.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential speech with explicit transition and contestability language.
contrary_evidence: This is rhetoric and self-presentation, not proof of actual electoral conduct.
The speech does not by itself rule out manipulation elsewhere in the system.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Buhari, who was constitutionally barred from contesting, would step down in 2023 after eight years and had told APC governors that he had no preferred candidate and had anointed no one.
evidence.title: Nigeria: Buhari has no preferred successor, spokesman says
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Buhari, who was constitutionally barred from contesting, would step down in 2023 after eight years and had told APC governors that he had no preferred candidate and had anointed no one.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with direct attribution and clear constitutional context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level succession behavior under Buhari, with the quote relayed through his spokesman.
contrary_evidence: Reuters reports a spokesperson's account, not a transcript of Buhari's own words.
No preferred successor does not prove complete neutrality in internal party competition.

evidence.claim: Buhari said fighting corruption remained a cardinal pillar of the administration, linked the Open Government Partnership to transparency in public finances and procurement, and said ICPC should continue investigating sexual harassment in educational institutions.
evidence.title: President Buhari’s Speech at the 4th National Summit on Diminishing Corruption in the Public Sector
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said fighting corruption remained a cardinal pillar of the administration, linked the Open Government Partnership to transparency in public finances and procurement, and said ICPC should continue investigating sexual harassment in educational institutions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential transcript; reliable for what he said, but self-report and not independent proof of practice.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari statement; strong attribution for rhetoric and commitments, weak for actual adherence.
contrary_evidence: Later 2022 nominations of loyal aides and relatives undercut the anti-nepotism and anti-patronage framing.

evidence.claim: Buhari directed cabinet members contesting elective office to resign by May 16, 2022 so they would not unfairly benefit from their government positions.
evidence.title: Nigeria’s Buhari asks ministers with political ambition to resign
evidence.excerpt: Buhari directed cabinet members contesting elective office to resign by May 16, 2022 so they would not unfairly benefit from their government positions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-syndicated report on a concrete directive and resulting resignations; strong for the fact of the rule, not for motive.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 during the election-cycle conflict-of-interest window.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari directive through his information minister; strong nexus to control of office and conflict separation.
contrary_evidence: The rule covered ministers only, not all appointees, so it did not eliminate broader patronage risks.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Buhari had no preferred APC successor and had anointed no one, and that he would step down in 2023 after eight years in office.
evidence.title: Nigeria: Buhari has no preferred successor, spokesman says
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Buhari had no preferred APC successor and had anointed no one, and that he would step down in 2023 after eight years in office.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report on a specific public statement by the president's spokesman; strong for the public commitment itself.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 ahead of the succession contest.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributed to Buhari through his spokesman; evidence supports a public non-anointment commitment, not hidden internal intent.
contrary_evidence: The statement does not prove he exerted no behind-the-scenes influence, only that he denied having a preferred candidate.

evidence.claim: The article says Buhari had appointed several family members and close relatives, and specifically notes that in September 2022 Ahmed Halilu, Aisha Buhari's brother, was appointed managing director of the Nigerian Security Printing and Minting Company.
evidence.title: Buhari's actions contradict nepotism comment
evidence.excerpt: The article says Buhari had appointed several family members and close relatives, and specifically notes that in September 2022 Ahmed Halilu, Aisha Buhari's brother, was appointed managing director of the Nigerian Security Printing and Minting Company.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Published commentary with a concrete appointment and family tie; the underlying appointment is corroborable, though the article is not a formal finding of illegality.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tied to Buhari's appointing power.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential appointment; strong nexus to Buhari's control over senior posts, though personal enrichment is not shown.
contrary_evidence: The article acknowledges that the president had constitutional discretion to appoint qualified people, so the appointment alone does not prove corruption or illegality.

evidence.claim: Buhari nominated his Special Assistant on Social Media, Lauretta Onochie, as substantive chair of the Niger Delta Development Commission and asked the Senate to confirm the appointment.
evidence.title: Buhari Nominates Lauretta Onochie As NDDC Chair, 14 Other Board Members
evidence.excerpt: Buhari nominated his Special Assistant on Social Media, Lauretta Onochie, as substantive chair of the Niger Delta Development Commission and asked the Senate to confirm the appointment.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct report of a concrete nomination with clear job history, strong for the appointment fact and loyalty nexus.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari nomination; the appointee was a close political aide, so the loyalty/patronage nexus is strong.
contrary_evidence: Onochie later denied partisan membership and supporters argued she was qualified, so the nomination is not itself proof of illegality.

evidence.claim: Buhari said weapons from the Ukraine-Russia war were beginning to filter into the Lake Chad Basin, but VOA's fact check found the claim unsubstantiated and noted there were no public reports or evidence supporting it.
evidence.title: Unsubstantiated: Buhari Claim That Ukraine War Feeds Arms to West Africa
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said weapons from the Ukraine-Russia war were beginning to filter into the Lake Chad Basin, but VOA's fact check found the claim unsubstantiated and noted there were no public reports or evidence supporting it.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct quote plus explicit fact-check with sourcing discussion; strong for the unsupported-claim assessment, weaker on intent.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari public statement; the fact check challenges the claim's evidentiary basis but cannot prove deliberate deception.
contrary_evidence: There is independent evidence of regional arms diversion from stockpiles and battlefield capture, but not of the specific Ukraine-to-Lake-Chad route Buhari asserted.

evidence.claim: Buhari approved Ahmed Halilu as substantive managing director of the Nigerian Security Printing and Minting Company, after Halilu had served in an acting role; the report says the appointment followed a CBN governor recommendation.
evidence.title: Buhari appoints Ahmed Halilu NSPMC MD
evidence.excerpt: Buhari approved Ahmed Halilu as substantive managing director of the Nigerian Security Printing and Minting Company, after Halilu had served in an acting role; the report says the appointment followed a CBN governor recommendation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous report with specific names and office, but secondary and dependent on unnamed CBN source.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and about a 2022 appointment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Buhari because the article says he approved the appointment; the CBN recommendation limits inference about sole presidential authorship.
contrary_evidence: Does not by itself prove nepotistic intent or personal benefit.
The report attributes the recommendation to the CBN governor and gives Halilu prior acting experience.

evidence.claim: The report says Ahmed Halilu, the elder brother to First Lady Aisha Buhari, was appointed managing director of NSPMC and that Buhari made the appointment permanent after Halilu had acted since May 16, 2022.
evidence.title: Buhari appoints brother-in-law, Ahmed Halilu, to head Nigeria's currency printing company
evidence.excerpt: The report says Ahmed Halilu, the elder brother to First Lady Aisha Buhari, was appointed managing director of NSPMC and that Buhari made the appointment permanent after Halilu had acted since May 16, 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report with a concrete family relationship and appointment fact, though it is still secondary reporting.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Buhari because the article states he made the appointment permanent; family relationship supports a nepotism reading but does not prove personal gain.
contrary_evidence: The article also notes Halilu's prior acting role and reported CBN backing, which support a competence-based explanation.
It does not show Buhari personally profited from the appointment.

evidence.claim: Buhari said weapons used in the Russia-Ukraine war were beginning to filter into the Lake Chad region and warned that the illegal movement of arms was heightening the proliferation of small arms and light weapons.
evidence.title: President Buhari Calls for Tighter Security Around Borders in Lake Chad Basin with the Proliferation of Weapons from Russia-Ukraine War
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said weapons used in the Russia-Ukraine war were beginning to filter into the Lake Chad region and warned that the illegal movement of arms was heightening the proliferation of small arms and light weapons.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential press release quoting Buhari directly on the disputed claim.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Buhari because this is his quoted public statement, though it does not itself prove the factual claim was true.
contrary_evidence: VOA later found the claim unsubstantiated and noted there were no public reports supporting it.
I did not locate any public correction by Buhari in the searched record.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 Buhari decision on nuclear brinkmanship, command-and-control, or other existential-risk use of presidential authority.
No independent audit of whether the 2021-2022 safeguards and physical-protection framework was actually implemented in practice.
No direct evidence of Buhari personally directing external military operations, proxy conduct, or coercive cross-border action in 2022.
No substantive mediation track or concrete ceasefire result led by Buhari himself.
Independent, case-level follow-through on prosecutions and investigations for major 2022 abuses is thin.
Some severe insecurity items are still better understood as state failure in a violent environment than as direct ruler-directed violence.
No independent pre-election audit of how fully the Electoral Act 2022 was implemented before the 2023 polls.
Much of the affirmative evidence is self-description from Buhari and his administration.
Budget execution and capital-spending delivery are not independently audited at the project level here.
Household-level and regional distributional causality remains only partially evidenced.
Independent audit evidence on how much of the announced welfare and health delivery actually reached beneficiaries in 2022 is limited.
The chapter still mixes federal action, donor support, and inherited deprivation.
No direct 2022 evidence of Buhari's assets, procurement benefits, bribes, or formal audit/court findings tied to personal enrichment.
The family-appointment case is strong on patronage but still thin on Buhari's knowledge, benefit, and intent beyond approval.
The Lake Chad arms claim is shown as unsupported, but there is no public correction or retraction by Buhari in the package.
Independent audit-grade evidence on the delivery tracker and the administration's correction of weak implementers is still limited.
The chapter still depends heavily on macro outcomes that mix Buhari-era policy with inherited constraints and external shocks.
